newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA DOUBLES LIMIT FOR SAVINGS COVERAGE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA DOUBLES LIMIT FOR SAVINGS COVERAGE.

text.p: Romania has doubled to 20.12 million lei ($2,700) the limit for individual depositors' savings coverage to adjust it with inflation in the first six months of this year, a central bank (BNR) statement said on Monday.
"The new threshold (of 20.12 million lei) is valid for the second half of the year," a BNR statement said.

It said the new limit would help cover about 96 percent of small depositors' savings in the case that a bank might face liquidation, with only 3.6 percent of individual bank depositors holding deposits larger than 20 million lei.
An insurance deposit system for small bank depositors approved last year had previously set the limit at 10 million lei. But it also said the limit should be adjusted with inflation every year.
Monthly inflation soared to an all-time high of 30.7 percent in March before falling to a record low of 0.7 percent last month. Inflation was 101.2 percent in June from end-1996.
The mandatory scheme, approved after Romania's banking sector was hit by defaults in two troubled banks, raises funds from all banks operating in the Balkan country.
Romania now has 40 commercial banks, of which eight are branches of foreign banks. Previously only the state savings bank had offered guarantees for its depositors.
Trouble at private banks Dacia Felix and Credit Bank flared in the past two years after they revealed huge losses and debts. Both banks await now court rulings on their liquidation or restructuring.
-- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264 ($ = 7450 Romanian Lei)
